The choice of mechanism turns on whether the audience signs in as editors do.
Section heading.
A staff-shaped audience restricted to one admin corner should use a none-capability role with its own home.
Such users are rows in the AUTH_DB editor table.
They are invited and removed through the same screen as editors.
The role path is the default for a small, editor-trusted audience sharing the invite flow.
A separate population needing its own login should not be modeled in the editor roster.
createAuthChannel is a separate login with its own D1 store, never AUTH_DB.
The channel has its own session, resolved by hashed lookup like the admin session.
The site builds the member area itself outside /admin; the channel ships no UI.
Nothing plugs into CairnAdminShell because channel sessions are not editor sessions.

locals.cairnEditor populates the same way for a none-capability session.

Section heading.
createAuthChannel builds request, confirm, and logout actions over a code of 8 to 10 digits.
The channel takes a delivery function and other required config.
Its D1 binding is never AUTH_DB.
Snippet: a member channel built from delivery, lookup, normalize, and challenge functions.
lookup and verify take an env context so a roster read reaches its own binding.
Neither may read request data; lookup decides membership and verify false destroys the session.
normalize, lookup, and challenge carry obligations the factory cannot verify.
